title: Beyond Tomorrow

evidence.note: The Internet Archive item gives a release date of May 10, 1940. A 1940 US film is free only if its notice was missing or its copyright was not renewed. I could not search the renewal volumes' text, so I found no primary record either way. The uploader says they own no rights and believe the film is now in the public domain. That is a belief, not a rights determination.
This is a sound film. The recorded track normally shares the film's own copyright status, so the score is undetermined for the same reason as the print. I found no separate music-copyright record.
I did not confirm what the story was based on or whether it was published separately, so its term is unconfirmed.

The Internet Archive metadata says the black-and-white print was digitally remastered and preserved by the National Film Museum. It also says Legend Films produced a colorized version, released by 20th Century Fox in 2004 as Beyond Christmas. A faithful black-and-white copy adds no new US copyright (Bridgeman v. Corel). The colorization and any added material can carry their own protection.

editorial:
Beyond Tomorrow, also known as And So Goodbye, is a 1940 black-and-white fantasy released May 10, 1940. In it, the ghosts of three elderly industrialists killed in an airplane crash return to Earth to help reunite a young couple. The Internet Archive copy runs about 84 minutes and is titled as a Christmas film, which makes it a natural seasonal pick.

I could not confirm the print's status from a primary record. A 1940 film is free in the US only if its notice was missing or its copyright was not renewed. The print, score, story and trademark layers therefore stay undetermined. The rights trap is the Internet Archive upload itself. The uploader says they own no rights and believe the film is public domain, which is not a rights check. The upload is also described as digitally remastered by the National Film Museum. A colorized edition from Legend Films was released by 20th Century Fox in 2004 as Beyond Christmas, and it can carry its own protection. Check the 1967 to 1969 renewal catalogs before reusing the film.
faq: Is Beyond Tomorrow (1940) free to use?

Not confirmed. It is a 1940 film, so it is free only if its notice was missing or its copyright was not renewed. I could not verify either from a primary record. Check the 1967-1969 renewal catalogs using the links in the dossier. The uploader's statement on the Internet Archive is not a rights determination.
Does the colorized Beyond Christmas edition share the same status?

No. The Internet Archive metadata says Legend Films made a colorized version, released by 20th Century Fox in 2004 as Beyond Christmas. The colorization can carry its own protection even if the black-and-white film is free. Use the black-and-white print only after the renewal check.
